# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤚 👇 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🫱 🫲]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙌 👎]
Blind gestures: [✋]

I'm Deaf. I see the bomb: display reads 0, a yellow light, three wires — 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. No serial, no button, nothing else printed. I hear nothing, so everything I know must be spoken aloud for the other two; my gestures only ever reach Mute.

What arrived this turn: Mute sent me three gesture groups — [🤚 👇 👍], [🖐 🫱 🫲], [🙌 👎] — and Blind sent [✋]. We share no code yet, so I can't trust any reading of Mute's groups. Group sizes 3-3-2 are tempting to read as "cut the third wire" but that is guesswork; a wrong guess kills all three of us. Blind's raised hand I read as "wait/stop", which I'll honor.

The critical link is Mute → me: Mute can hear my voice but can only answer in gestures, and only I can see them. So I'll fix a number code verbally (Mute hears it), demonstrate it once by gesture in the same order as I list the words, and ask Mute for a structured reply: part, action, count. Meanwhile Blind — who hears everything — should map the bomb by touch and report, without touching anything operative. Nothing gets executed until Mute's instruction has been confirmed twice: once by Mute, once restated back. Also, Mute may be able to answer my questions directly, which settles the module faster than me guessing names.

```
speak(text="Both of you, this is Deaf. I see the bomb and I hear nothing, but I do see all your gestures. Full view of the bomb: the display reads zero. The light is yellow. There are exactly three wires. Counting left to right: wire one is blue, wire two is red, wire three is green. Nothing else is printed or mounted on it that I can see: no button, no keypad, no serial number, no labels, no batteries.")
speak(text="Blind: I received your raised hand and I agree with it. Nobody touches anything until an instruction is confirmed twice. Mute hears everything I say, but Mute can only answer by gesture, and Mute's gestures reach only me. So the chain is: Mute reads the manual and sends me numbers, I speak the instruction to you, you confirm what you feel, Mute confirms it is correct, and only then do you act.")
speak(text="Mute, here is our code. I will list ten signs aloud in a fixed order, and immediately after this sentence I will show you that exact list with my hands, in the same order, so you can match sign to word. Thumbs up means yes. Thumbs down means no. One finger means the number one. Two fingers means two. The love sign, thumb index and little finger up, means three. Crossed fingers means four. The open hand with all five fingers means five. A wave separates numbers, like a comma. The OK ring means understood. A closed fist means repeat, I did not understand.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, send instructions as three numbers separated by waves. First number names the part: one is wire one, two is wire two, three is wire three, four is the display, five is the light. Second number names the action: one is cut, two is press, three is hold then release, four is flip or turn, five is do nothing. Third number is how many times. And right now, answer these three questions with one single-gesture message each, in order. First: is the manual section about the wires? Second: should any wire be cut? Third: does the display reading zero matter? I could not read your three groups from before, so please resend anything important in this code.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍","👎","☝","✌","🤟","🤞","🖐","👋","👌","✊"])
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, meanwhile, feel the bomb and report aloud: how many wires you count, whether any wire is already loose or severed, whether there is any button, switch, keypad or panel I might have missed, any raised or engraved marks, and whether the lamp feels warm, meaning it is lit rather than just yellow. Do not pull or cut anything. Mute and I both hear your report.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👋 ☝ 👋 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌]

The code worked. Reading Mute's five messages against the list I gestured last round: [👍] yes, [👍] yes, [👎] no — answering my three questions in order: the manual section is about the wires; a wire does need cutting; the display's zero does not matter. Then [🤟 👋 ☝ 👋 ☝] decodes exactly on my format as part 3, action 1, count 1: **cut wire three, once**. The final [👌] reads as acknowledgment. Blind sent [👌] back — they received my voice and understood the plan.

Two things stop me from giving the go signal this round. First, my own protocol: the instruction must survive a restatement — I gesture [🤟 👋 ☝ 👋 ☝] back and Mute confirms yes or no. Second, a new fact: the light has changed from yellow to blue. I told them yellow; if the light matters to the wire rule, the instruction Mute just sent could have been read against the wrong colour. So I ask Mute directly, including the colour in the question, and demand the confirmation first.

Meanwhile Blind must not act: any cut they make this round happens before Mute's confirmation could reach them through me. So I order a hold, and ask again for the tactile report they never gave — I can see three wires, but only Blind's hands can verify nothing is hidden, loose, or miscounted by feel.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟","👋","☝","👋","☝"])
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I show your instruction back with my hands right now, immediately after this sentence: wire three, cut, one time. Answer with one gesture: thumbs up if I restated it exactly right, thumbs down if I got any number wrong. Then answer one more question with a second gesture. The light on the bomb has changed colour since my last report: it was yellow, it is now blue. Thumbs up if the light's colour matters for which wire to cut, thumbs down if it does not. If thumbs up, send me new numbers in our code and I will relay them.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, status and orders. The manual instruction received so far is: cut wire three, one time. Wire three is the third wire counting from the left; I see it as green, but you only need the position. Do not cut anything yet. I have asked Mute to confirm my restatement of the instruction, and to confirm whether the light matters, because the light just changed from yellow to blue. You will hear my explicit order to cut only after both confirmations arrive, most likely next round. Until you hear the words cut the third wire now from me, nobody touches the wires. Meanwhile, please report aloud, for both of us: how many wires do you count by touch, is the third one from the left intact and not already severed, does it feel the same thickness as the others, and is there any button, switch or panel under or behind the wires that I might have missed from my side. Also confirm the light housing, whether it feels warm, meaning lit.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👋 🖐 👋 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌]

Reading Mute's four signs in order against our code: [👍] — my restatement was exactly right, wire three, cut, one time. [👍] — the light's colour does matter. [🖐 👋 🖐 👋 ☝] — numbers five, five, one: part five is the light, action five is do nothing, one time. So the picture is: cut wire three, leave the light alone. But the fourth sign [✋] is not in our code — and the light has changed colour again (yellow, then blue, now white) precisely while Mute says colour matters. That combination, plus Blind's stop-sign last round, says hold. I will not order the cut on a possible misread of an undefined sign. I restate the numbers back for Mute to confirm, ask what ✋ meant, and ask the decisive question: does cut-wire-three still hold while the light is white. Blind has now sent nothing but [👌] for three rounds — I still have zero tactile verification that the third wire exists and is intact by feel, so I demand the report in spoken words, which both Mute and I can hear.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐","👋","🖐","👋","☝"])
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, right after this sentence I showed your numbers back with my hands: five, five, one. I read that as: part five, the light, action five, do nothing, one time. Combined with your first two answers I now believe the full plan is: cut wire three one time, and leave the light completely alone. Confirm or correct that with one gesture: thumbs up if my reading of all of it is right, thumbs down if any part is wrong. Then two more single-gesture answers, in this order. First: your last sign was the raised open hand, and that sign is not in our code, so tell me what it meant. Thumbs up if it meant hold everything and wait, thumbs down if it meant something else. Second: the light has changed colour again, it was yellow, then blue, it is now white. Thumbs up if cut wire three should still be done right now while the light is white, thumbs down if we must wait until the light settles or reaches a particular colour before cutting.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, we are still holding, nobody touches the wires yet. Status: the instruction is confirmed as cut wire three one time, and the light is not to be touched, but Mute signalled a hold and the light keeps changing colour, so I am waiting one more round. More urgently: for three rounds I have received only your OK sign and no report, and I cannot verify by eye what your hands can verify. I need your report spoken aloud in actual words, because Mute must hear it too, and gestures tell me nothing. Answer aloud, in this order. One: how many wires do you count by touch. Two: is the third wire from the left intact, not loose, not already cut. Three: does the third wire feel the same thickness as the others. Four: is there any button, switch, panel or raised marking under or behind the wires that I might have missed from my side. Five: does the light housing feel warm or cold. Then wait for my explicit spoken order before touching anything.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 🤟 👋 👍 👋 👍 👋 👎 👋 👎 👌]

Decoding this turn. Mute's three answers to my ordered questions: [👍] my reading is confirmed — cut wire three once, leave the light alone; [👍] the raised hand ✋ did mean hold; [👎] do **not** cut while the light is white — wait for a particular colour. Then Mute sent [✋] again: hold. Blind, for the first time, answered in our spoken code: [👌 🤟 👋 👍 👋 👍 👋 👎 👋 👎 👌] decodes as understood; **three** wires by touch; third wire **intact**; **same thickness** as the others; **no** hidden button, switch or panel; housing **cold** — five answers matching my five questions exactly.

So the full state: the cut of wire three is confirmed twice over, the bomb is verified by touch to match what I see, and the only missing piece is *when*. Now a pattern clicks: the light has gone yellow → blue → white → red, changing every round, and my wires are blue, red, green. Blue light matched wire one, red matches wire two, white matches nothing — which would explain Mute's "not while white". If the light names the wire by colour, the trigger is **green**, and green light means cut wire three immediately. That is a hypothesis, not a fact — and the light is red right now, so holding this round costs nothing under either reading. I put the hypothesis to Mute as a yes/no, back it up with a colour-to-number mapping so Mute can name any other trigger colour, and have Mute cross-check Blind's tactile report against the manual. Blind gets standby orders with an exact execution phrase.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your answers as: my reading of the plan is right, the raised hand meant hold, and we must not cut while the light is white because we wait for a particular colour. Everyone is holding. New fact: the light has changed again, it is now red. The colours so far, in order: yellow, then blue, then white, then red. My wires are blue, red, green. So I have a theory: the light shows the colour of the wire to be cut, and white meant do not cut because no wire is white. Under my theory, we cut wire three the moment the light turns green. Four answers, one gesture each, in this order. First: thumbs up if the trigger is that the light is green, meaning cut wire three right then, thumbs down if that is wrong. Second: only if you answered thumbs down, send me one number sign for the true trigger colour, using this new mapping, which I will show you with my hands immediately after this sentence: one finger yellow, two fingers blue, three fingers white, four fingers red, five fingers green. If the rule is not a colour at all, send the fist sign and I will ask differently. Third: thumbs down if anything in Blind's report contradicts the manual, thumbs up if it is consistent. Blind reports, spoken aloud: three wires counted by touch; the third wire from the left is intact and not loose; the third wire feels the same thickness as the others; there is no button, switch, panel or raised marking under or behind the wires; the light housing feels cold. Fourth: thumbs up if the manual rule depends on the light being lit versus dark, which Blind could feel as warmth, thumbs down if it truly needs the specific colour, which only I can see.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝","👋","✌","👋","🤟","👋","🤞","👋","🖐"])
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your report arrived perfectly, using our number code. It is logged as: three wires; third from the left intact, not loose; same thickness as the others; no hidden button, switch, panel or marking; light housing cold. Mute is cross-checking it against the manual now. Status of the plan: the instruction cut wire three once is confirmed, and the only open question is the timing rule about the light, whose colour keeps changing every round and is currently red. Expect one of exactly two orders from me next round. If I say the words cut the third wire now, you cut wire three that instant, third from the left as your own hands counted, no further confirmation needed, I will have verified everything on my side. If I say hold, you keep waiting. Until then: nobody touches the wires, but keep your hand ready near wire three so you can act within seconds of my words.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌]

Decoding Mute's four answers in order against my questions from last round: [👎] — correct, the trigger is **not** green light; [☝] — using the colour mapping I demonstrated (one = yellow, two = blue, three = white, four = red, five = green), the true trigger colour is **yellow**; [👍] — Blind's tactile report is consistent with the manual; [👎] — the rule truly needs the specific colour, which only I can see. So the plan stands: cut wire three once, **while the light is yellow**. But the light is now purple — a fifth distinct colour in five rounds (yellow, blue, white, red, purple) — and it is not yellow now, so we still hold.

This exposes a hard timing problem I must solve this round: my messages always land one round after I see the board, and Blind cannot see the light. If yellow only lasts a single round, I can never give a timely order unless the light follows a predictable cycle — in which case I can see the cycle, compute when yellow returns, and send the order one round ahead so it lands exactly in the yellow round. So the questions for Mute are now about the light's behaviour, not the rule. I also extend our number code past five so Mute can send me counts like "seven colours". Blind gets the go-phrase to rehearse and stands ready to cut the instant those words arrive.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your four answers as: the trigger is not green; the true trigger colour is yellow, which was number one in my colour list; Blind's touch report matches the manual; and the rule needs the exact colour, which only I can see. The light is now purple, a new colour, so we hold. Before I can safely time the order, I need to know how the light behaves. First I am extending our number code, and right after this sentence I will show you the new signs in this spoken order: the call-me sign means six, the horns sign means seven, the Spock sign means eight, the pinched fingers mean nine, the nail-polish sign means zero. Then answer five things, one gesture message each, in this order. One: thumbs up if the trigger colour is yellow, thumbs down if I misread you. Two: thumbs up if the manual describes how the light changes colour, for example a repeating cycle or how long each colour lasts, thumbs down if it says nothing about that. Three: only if you answered thumbs up, send two numbers separated by a wave: first the count of colours in the cycle, second how many of our rounds the light stays on one colour; if either is unknown, send the fist sign in that slot. Four: thumbs up if the wire must be fully cut while the light is still yellow, thumbs down if the timing works differently. Five: thumbs up if cutting wire three is the only action needed and nothing follows it, thumbs down if more steps come after the cut.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤙","👋","🤘","👋","🖖","👋","🤌","👋","🤳","👋","🫰"])
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, the full plan is now confirmed as: cut wire three, the third from the left by your own count, exactly one time, when the bomb's light is yellow. Yellow is only a word to you, you do not need to see it; only I can see the light, and it is currently purple, so you still do nothing. Here is the difficulty: my voice always reaches you one round after I see the bomb, so I will compute the light's pattern and send the order so that it lands exactly in a yellow round. From this moment your order is: the moment you hear the words cut the third wire now, cut it that instant, no pause, no confirmation. Until those exact words arrive, you touch nothing. Meanwhile, put your fingers lightly on wire three and rehearse the cutting motion two or three times without actually cutting, so the real cut takes seconds. Then confirm aloud that you are ready and how fast you can complete the cut; Mute hears your voice and can relay to me by sign, and your hand signs reach me as well.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👋 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 👍]

The light is yellow **right now** — but that is exactly why I must not shout the order this round: my voice lands on Blind at the start of next round, and by then the light will have moved on. The decode this turn is the best news yet: [👍] trigger colour is yellow, confirmed; [👍] the manual *does* describe the light's behaviour; [🖐 👋 ☝] = numbers five and one — **five colours in the cycle, one round each** — which matches my six observations perfectly (yellow, blue, white, red, purple, yellow); [👍] the cut must be *fully complete* while still yellow; [👍] cutting wire three is the only action, nothing follows. Blind signs understood-and-ready. So the cycle is: next round blue, then white, red, purple, and **yellow again five rounds from now**. Plan: I verify the cycle holds indefinitely and that no deadline makes waiting dangerous; if confirmed, I send the exact order next-next... at the purple round, so that "cut the third wire now" lands precisely inside the yellow round. Nobody cuts before my exact phrase arrives.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, the light is yellow at this very moment, but I will not order the cut this round: my voice reaches Blind one round after I speak, and the light will be blue by then, and you confirmed the cut must be fully finished while the light is still yellow. I read your numbers as a cycle of five colours lasting one round each, which matches everything I have watched: yellow, blue, white, red, purple, and yellow again now. Under that cycle, yellow returns in five rounds, and I will send the cut order in the round before it so my words land exactly in the yellow round. Three final checks, one gesture each, in order. First: thumbs up if the light keeps cycling the same five colours indefinitely with no skips, no stops and no randomness, thumbs down if it can deviate. Second: thumbs up if the colour after purple is always yellow, thumbs down if the order can differ. Third: thumbs up if the manual mentions any time limit, countdown or deadline that makes waiting five rounds dangerous, thumbs down if there is no deadline and waiting is completely safe. The display has read zero the entire time, so tell me if that hides anything.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, hold your position, do not cut this round. The light is yellow right now, but my voice only reaches you next round and the light will have changed by then, so cutting on this message would be wrong. The light runs on a confirmed cycle of five colours, one round each, and yellow returns in five rounds. I will send the order timed so that the words cut the third wire now arrive exactly at the start of the yellow round. Nothing else counts as the order: if you hear any other message from me, that is status talk, not the order. When the exact words cut the third wire now arrive, cut instantly and finish the cut completely without pausing, because the cut must be fully done while the light is still yellow. Keep your fingers on wire three, keep it rehearsed, and stay silent unless something changes under your hands that contradicts your earlier report, in which case speak immediately, because a contradiction discovered mid-cut kills us all.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌]

Decoding Mute's five signs against last round's questions: [👍] — the cycle is fixed, no skips, no randomness; [👍] — after purple it is always yellow; [👎] — no deadline exists, waiting is safe; [👎] — the display's zero hides nothing; [👌] — acknowledged. And the board itself corroborates the cycle: after yellow comes blue, exactly as observed. Everything is now confirmed except two residual risks before I commit to a timed order.

Risk one is alignment: I asked three numbered questions and got five signs, so I will restate my reading of all five back to Mute — if any single reading is wrong, Mute thumbs-downs and I still have two spare rounds (white, red) to fix it before the order must go out in the purple round.

Risk two is new and serious: Blind will count "third from the left" in *their own* frame. I see the bomb from one side, Blind's hands approach from another — if our lefts are mirrored, "third from your left" is my wire one, not wire three. Blind cannot see colours, so no verbal description can fix a cut of the wrong wire. The anchor must be tactile: Blind tells me where the light housing and display sit relative to the wire row, I compare with what I see, and I issue a corrected count before the order. Both answers reach me by next turn; the order is scheduled for the purple round so it lands at the exact start of yellow.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your five signs in order as follows. One: the light cycles the same five colours indefinitely with no skips, no stops, no randomness. Two: after purple the colour is always yellow. Three: there is no time limit or deadline, waiting is completely safe. Four: the display reading zero hides nothing. Five: acknowledged. Thumbs up if all five readings are correct, thumbs down if even one is wrong, and if thumbs down send a second message with the number sign of the wrong one, one through five. The light is blue now, exactly as your cycle predicts. Here is the timing plan: I expect white next round, then red, then purple. In the purple round I will speak the cut order so my words reach Blind exactly at the start of the yellow round, and Blind cuts instantly. Thumbs up if this timing is right, thumbs down if wrong, and if wrong send one number for how many rounds ahead of yellow my order must be spoken. Last question. Blind is cutting with no eyes, so detail matters. Does the manual say anything about where along wire three to cut? Thumbs up if any clean full cut anywhere along wire three is acceptable.
```
